blocks.text: HBL Engineering Limited (formerly HBL Power Systems Limited; name changed on 13 November 2024) designs and manufactures specialised industrial batteries, defence and aviation batteries, and railway and defence electronics, from plants concentrated in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. [F] (AR2025 p.46) Its statutory reportable segments are Batteries and Electronics, with Defence & Aviation disclosed separately in the segment note and other activities grouped as unallocated. [F] (AR2025 p.268)

Management describes the company as nine operating divisions grouped into three business segments: Industrial Batteries (lead acid VRLA/PLT, nickel cadmium, lithium), Defence Businesses (batteries for aircraft, missiles, torpedoes and submarines; electronic fuzes for ammunition; other defence products) and Industrial Electronics (rail signalling including Kavach and TMS/CTC; electric drive trains; other products in exploratory stage). [MC] (AR2025 p.4) The money is made by selling engineered hardware into specification-locked niches where qualification, not price, is the entry barrier, and, in rail signalling, by executing tendered supply-and-installation contracts for Indian Railways. [AI] (AR2025 p.5; AR2025 p.12)

**The revenue base changed shape completely in FY26.** Consolidated sales rose from Rs 1,967 crore in FY25 to Rs 3,303 crore in FY26 (+67.9%) and EBITDA from Rs 393 crore to Rs 1,113 crore, lifting the operating margin from 20% to 34%. [F] (NUMBERS) The screener profile attributes roughly 49% of FY26 revenue to the Industrial Electronics segment against about 15% in FY25, with Kavach alone around half of FY26 sales. [F] (SCREENER) That concentration is the single most important fact in this report. [AI] (SCREENER; NUMBERS)

subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: This is not a recent listing. The company has been listed on BSE and NSE for decades, has 27,71,94,946 shares of Re 1 outstanding, unchanged through FY25, and 99.25% of capital is dematerialised. [F] (AR2025 p.44; AR2025 p.52) There is therefore no lock-in expiry or IPO-proceeds overhang to analyse; the constraint on this report is disclosure quality, not listing history. [AI] (AR2025 p.52)

Evidence-base limitations, stated plainly: the most recent annual report available to us is FY25; the FY26 annual report was circulated on 3 September 2026 ahead of the 40th AGM on 26 September 2026 but is not in our document set [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). The only transcript available is the 39th AGM of 25 September 2025 - there are no quarterly earnings-call transcripts in our evidence base [F] (CALL Sep 2025). The most recent investor presentation is dated September 2023 [F] (PPT Sep 2023). Consequently FY26 and Q1 FY27 are visible only as numbers, with no segment split, no order-book update from the company itself and no management commentary. A prospectus or detailed-project report was not available.

The company does not publish an order book in any document we hold. Every order-book figure in this report comes from the credit rating agency's February 2026 press release, which sources it from the company. [F] (RATING) That is a second-hand disclosure channel and should be treated as such. [AI] (RATING)

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. The price sits far above every fair value our model produces: Rs 760 versus bear Rs 123.3, base Rs 239.5 and bull Rs 354.8 per share, that is -83.8%, -68.5% and -53.3% respectively [F] (NUMBERS). Even the most generous cell of the sensitivity grid (WACC 13.5%, terminal growth 6.5%) gives Rs 320.5 [F] (NUMBERS).

2. The reverse DCF requires about 58.9% annual sales growth for five years to justify today's enterprise value, against 19.5% in the base case [F] (NUMBERS). Management's own FY30 ambition of Rs 4,500 crore implies growth in the high single digits from the FY26 base [E] (AR2025 p.5; NUMBERS).

3. Earnings are already rolling over. Quarterly OPM went 44% (Sep-25), 35% (Dec-25), 12% (Mar-26), 23% (Jun-26), and Q1 FY27 profit after tax fell 23.8% year on year on 6.0% sales growth [F] (NUMBERS). Annualising Q1 FY27 gives roughly Rs 2,552 crore against FY26's Rs 3,303 crore [E] (NUMBERS).

4. The disclosed order book is shrinking: Rs 2,999 crore at 31 December 2025 against Rs 4,479 crore at 31 July 2025, a 33% fall in five months [F] (RATING). Book-to-bill on FY26 sales is roughly 0.91x [E] (RATING; NUMBERS).

5. Kavach concentration is effectively single-customer exposure. Around half of FY26 sales came from Kavach [F] (SCREENER), and the buyer is Indian Railways. Contract terms bite: HBL supplied 76% of the CLW locomotive order within the execution window ending mid-December 2025 and the balance stands cancelled [F] (RATING).

6. Management guides to a plateau, not compounding: Kavach sales steady at Rs 1,300-1,500 crore per year in FY26, FY27 and FY28 and dipping later [MC] (AR2025 p.5), with a possible decline in FY28 [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). The bridge to FY30 depends on products not yet sold commercially [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

7. The legacy battery base is structurally shrinking in its largest end market. The company itself plans to prune 2V-VRLA capacity as telecom shifts to lithium, and expects considerable revenue reduction in FY26 and beyond in that line [F] (AR2025 p.5). Lead acid capacity utilisation fell to 54% in FY25 from 68% [F] (RATING).

8. Working capital intensity absorbs the growth. Cash conversion cycle was 171 days in FY26 and 202 days in FY25 [F] (NUMBERS); the rating agency puts the FY25 operating cycle at 147 days against 114 days in FY24 [F] (RATING). In the base-case model, year-one free cash flow to the firm is only Rs 197 crore on Rs 864 crore of EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS).

9. Governance is founder-dependent and expensively aligned. The Chairman and Managing Director, aged 79 as disclosed in the FY25 report and born 3 November 1945, took Rs 19.98 crore in FY25 of which Rs 18.95 crore was commission on profits, about 7.1% of standalone profit after tax [F] (AR2025 p.50; AR2025 p.42) [E] (AR2025 p.50). The stated succession plan is explicitly not to appoint a single CEO [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

10. Disclosure candour is thin for a company of this size: no company-published order book, no installed-capacity disclosure, no quarterly earnings calls in our evidence base, and the last investor presentation is from September 2023 [F] (PPT Sep 2023) [AI] (AR2025; CALL Sep 2025).
11. Institutional validation is largely absent: domestic institutions held 0.97% and foreign institutions 5.62% at June 2026, the latter down from 7.10% in September 2025 [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: Our variant perception is not about whether HBL is a good business - the returns on capital, the qualification barriers and the absence of debt make that case adequately. It is about what is being paid for and what is actually contracted. The market appears to be extrapolating a year in which a two-decade R&D project (Kavach) converted into roughly half of revenue at an execution-phase margin, into a compounding franchise. The company's own documents describe something flatter: Kavach revenue steady for three years then dipping [MC] (AR2025 p.5), a legacy telecom battery business being deliberately pruned [F] (AR2025 p.5), and a FY30 total-company ambition of Rs 4,500 crore [MC] (AR2025 p.5) that is only modestly above FY26 actuals of Rs 3,303 crore [F] (NUMBERS). Meanwhile the price requires about 58.9% annual sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS). The asymmetry we see is therefore between a high-quality, narrowly-based industrial company and a price that already assumes the next three Kavachs have been invented, qualified and ordered. [AI] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.5)

subsections.title: What the timeline reveals about how recent the business really is

blocks.text: Two readings coexist. The corporate entity is forty years old, the nickel cadmium franchise dates from the late 1970s and the aircraft and missile battery positions have been held for decades [MC] (PPT Sep 2023). But **the business that produces today's profits is barely two years old in revenue terms**: Kavach R&D started in 2005, was demonstrated in 2012, was certified to v4.0 only in May 2025, and became roughly half of revenue in FY26 [F] (AR2025 p.12; SCREENER). [AI] (AR2025 p.12)

Management's own framing is that conception-to-profit has averaged fifteen years and Kavach took twenty [MC] (AR2025 p.5). Applied consistently, that timeline says the next leg (electronic fuzes started 2005, torpedo motors, electric trucks started 2017, marine propulsion started 2026) will deliver over FY28-FY30, not FY27 [AI] (AR2025 p.5; PPT Sep 2023; SCREENER). The investment question is therefore whether the price is paying for the twenty-year-old success that has already arrived or for pipeline products whose revenue is, today, zero [AI] (NUMBERS).

sections.title: Business model: how value is created and captured

items: Step 1 - Gap identification: management screens for products that India imports or assembles under foreign licence, on the judgment that a technology gap is a protected profit pool [MC] (AR2025 p.4)

Step 2 - In-house R&D, self-funded and largely expensed: R&D not eligible for capitalisation was Rs 9.72 crore in FY25 and Rs 12.19 crore in FY24 on a standalone basis [F] (AR2025 p.170); the internally generated new product development intangible of Rs 56.15 crore is fully amortised [F] (AR2025 p.169)

Step 3 - Qualification: RDSO certification for Kavach, DRDO/ARDE approvals for fuzes and grenades, FAA/EASA and OEM clearances for aviation batteries, Bureau Veritas SIL-2 for TMS [F] (AR2025 p.12; PPT Sep 2023)
Step 4 - In-house equipment and process build: the company states it designs its own production equipment to lower capital cost and make small volumes viable [MC] (AR2025 p.4)
Step 5 - Manufacture at six named sites plus a development centre, seven plants on the BRSR count [F] (AR2025 p.14; AR2025 p.101)
Step 6 - Sale, either by tender (Indian Railways, BSNL, MoD) or direct to OEMs and EPCs, with exports routed partly through the German and US subsidiaries [F] (PPT Sep 2023; RATING)

Step 7 - Installation and services for rail signalling: Rs 250.73 crore of FY25 consolidated revenue was sale of services, and Rs 201.71 crore of standalone revenue was recognised over time [F] (AR2025 p.252; AR2025 p.191); the EPC portion of TCAS contracts is subcontracted [F] (PPT Sep 2023)

Step 8 - Aftermarket: expected service life of a TCAS system is 15 years and the railways pay annually for maintenance after the first few years [MC] (PPT Sep 2023); batteries are replacement items with recurring demand [MC] (AR2025 p.8)

blocks.text: Value is captured at the qualification step, not the manufacturing step. In Kavach the certified content is roughly 70% of a TCAS contract with the remaining EPC scope subcontracted [F] (PPT Sep 2023); in defence batteries the MoD keeps a second source but pays a premium for small-volume Indian-made quality [MC] (AR2025 p.8; CALL Sep 2025); in Ni-Cd exports management says it prices about 20% below incumbent foreign brands and still earns a decent margin [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). Where qualification is absent or the product is commoditised - telecom VRLA, lithium cells, 155mm artillery fuzes - management has chosen to withdraw or not participate [F] (AR2025 p.5; AR2025 p.11) [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

The FY25 segment note supports this: computed segment operating margins were 48.6% for Defence & Aviation, 23.0% for Batteries and 11.9% for Electronics, with unallocated activities running at a Rs 50.35 crore operating loss [E] (AR2025 p.269). **The highest-margin segment is the smallest, and the segment that carried FY26 growth was the lowest-margin one in FY25** - which makes the FY26 34% consolidated margin an important thing to explain rather than to assume [AI] (AR2025 p.269; NUMBERS).

The model is capital-light by design and by evidence. Fixed assets net were Rs 441 crore on Rs 3,303 crore of FY26 sales, a fixed-asset turnover of 7.49x, with capex at 4.4% of sales in FY26 and 7.7% in FY25 [F] (NUMBERS). Cumulative capex over FY22-FY26 was Rs 436 crore against a Rs 2,391 crore increase in annual revenue between FY21 and FY26, an incremental revenue-to-capital ratio of about 5.5x [E] (NUMBERS). Capital work in progress stood at Rs 127 crore and capital commitments at Rs 68.13 crore at March 2025 [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.269).

The capital intensity that does exist sits in working capital, not plant. Inventory days were 148 in FY26 and 201 in FY25, against payable days of 49 and 68 [F] (NUMBERS); management built Kavach inventory six to eight months before holding a firm order and before v4.0 certification, a deliberate risk [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). Classification: **asset-light in fixed capital, working-capital-heavy in operation** [AI] (NUMBERS; RATING).

blocks.text: The client base is unusually high-quality for a company of this size - national defence services, a national railway, global rolling-stock and engine OEMs - and the relationships are qualification-based, which makes them durable. Wallet share is therefore structurally limited even where the technology is unique [AI] (CALL Sep 2025). Second, no customer-level revenue is disclosed anywhere, so stickiness cannot be quantified, only asserted [AI] (AR2025 p.244). Third, the fastest-growing relationship (Indian Railways) is also the one with the least pricing freedom, because Kavach pricing is set through tender and the lever is volume rather than price [AI] (CALL Sep 2025).

subsections.title: Kavach and rail signalling: the profit engine

blocks.text: Position in the value chain: HBL is a system OEM, not a component supplier. It co-developed the specification with RDSO from 2005 without RDSO funding, demonstrated it on track in October 2012, and its certified content is roughly 70% of a TCAS contract value with the EPC scope subcontracted [F] (AR2025 p.12; PPT Sep 2023). Interoperability with rival designs is mandatory and time-consuming to achieve, which is the real barrier for new entrants [F] (PPT Sep 2023).

What exists today versus narrative: what exists is certification (first to v4.0 on 13 May 2025), about Rs 4,000 crore of contracts won, a disclosed Rs 2,999 crore order book at December 2025, Rs 1,375 crore of fresh onboard orders, and roughly half of FY26 revenue [F] (AR2025 p.12; RATING; SCREENER). What is narrative is everything after FY28: management expects Kavach to dip and TMS/CTC plus fuzes to compensate [MC] (AR2025 p.5; CALL Sep 2025), while conceding TMS contracts will not be comparable in value to Kavach [MC] (AR2025 p.12).

Anchor-customer exposure, quantified: Indian Railways entities are the counterparty for approximately 50% of FY26 revenue [F] (SCREENER). Railways customer-category revenue was Rs 529.5 crore standalone in FY25, 27% of standalone turnover [E] (AR2025 p.191). The counterparty sets the specification (v3.2 to v4.0), the certification date (16 July 2024 freeze, 13 May 2025 HBL certification), the tender calendar and the cancellation terms - and has already exercised the last of these [F] (AR2025 p.12; RATING).

blocks.text: Strategic implication: the Kavach position is genuinely defensible on certification, and genuinely undiversifiable on customer. The three unqualified OEMs' orders may be forfeited and re-floated, which management says could come at the original prices rather than inflated ones [MC] (CALL Sep 2025) - that is the single largest identifiable swing factor for FY28 revenue, and it is entirely outside the company's control [AI] (CALL Sep 2025).

Value-chain position: HBL sits at the qualified-component layer. It is one of two Indian torpedo-battery suppliers, competes with Exide on submarine batteries through tender, supplies almost all IAF aircraft batteries, designed and manufactures most Indian missile batteries including for Agni V, and exports missile batteries to Israel and the UAE [MC] (PPT Sep 2023). In fuzes it claims to be the only company in India with 100% indigenisation, against ECIL and BEL which import the core components [MC] (AR2025 p.8; CALL Sep 2025).

blocks.text: Our answer is: **partly, and much less than the FY26 headline suggests.** Three components can be separated [AI] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.269). First, a structural mix gain of roughly 500-800 basis points, evidenced by the battery segment margin improvement, the doubling of high-margin defence exports and the permanent reduction in low-margin EPC works-contract revenue - this part of the FY24-to-FY25 improvement was achieved on falling sales, which is the strongest possible evidence that it is mix and not leverage [E] (AR2025 p.269; AR2025 p.219). Second, operating leverage on a largely fixed engineering and overhead base, which is real but reverses when volume falls - Q4 FY26 at 12% OPM demonstrates the reversal [F] (NUMBERS). Third, an execution-phase premium on Kavach, which by definition ends with the programme [AI] (RATING).

The practical test for FY27: our DCF base case assumes a 20% EBITDA margin against a 32% trailing margin [F] (NUMBERS). Q1 FY27 printed 23% [F] (NUMBERS). Two more quarters in the 22-26% range would say the structural gain is roughly 300-600 basis points above the pre-Kavach norm - materially better than the model assumes, but nowhere near the FY26 headline [AI] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: **Per-unit economics cannot be built from these disclosures.** There is no installed capacity in units, no volume produced or sold, no realisation per battery or per Kavach kilometre, and no price list in any document in our evidence base [AI] (AR2025; RATING). The only volume-adjacent disclosures are two utilisation percentages [F] (RATING) and a statement that Ni-Cd pocket plate business grew more than 30% in FY25 with volume growth across all user segments [F] (AR2025 p.10). A blended realisation or contribution-per-unit table would require us to invent either the denominator or the split, so we do not present one.
What can be built is a cost structure per rupee of revenue, which is disclosed in full for FY24 and FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.219).

blocks.text: Three separate breaks sit between any of these figures and HBL's revenue. First, **the award mechanism**: Kavach work is tendered in rounds to at least five approved OEMs, so a national kilometre target is not an HBL order book [F] (AR2025 p.12) [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). In fairness, the reverse DCF is computed at the base-case 20% EBITDA margin [F] (NUMBERS), while the business has just delivered 34% for a full year and 23% in the most recent quarter [F] (NUMBERS). A reverse DCF at a materially higher sustained margin would require materially less growth to justify the same enterprise value - the model does not publish that variant, and we will not construct one [AI] (NUMBERS). Three further points cut the same way: the enterprise value is not netted for cash or the Rs 402 crore investment book [F] (NUMBERS); the capex rule assumes worse capital efficiency than the company has actually achieved [E] (NUMBERS); and the terminal value carries 78% of the base case, so a 5.5% perpetual growth assumption for a company with these returns on capital may be the binding conservatism [E] (NUMBERS).

Taken together, an investor who believes the FY26 margin is 80% structural and that Kavach is followed by fuzes at similar economics can build a far higher number than Rs 239.5. What they cannot do on this evidence base is bridge from Rs 354.8 - the bull case, with a 22% margin and 42.7% starting growth - to Rs 760, because **the gap is not a margin argument, it is a growth argument, and no disclosed order book, guidance or management statement supports 58.9%** [AI] (NUMBERS; RATING; AR2025 p.5).

blocks.text: Summary research view: a high-quality, cash-generative, approval-moated industrial whose FY26 earnings were produced by a single programme in its execution phase, trading above the fair value implied by every scenario in our model. The operating evidence is strong; the valuation evidence is not; and the disclosure evidence is too thin to settle the argument in either direction without the FY26 annual report [AI] (NUMBERS; AR2025; RATING).

There is no prior report for this company in this dashboard, so this is initial coverage and there is no quarter-on-quarter change log. The baseline we establish for the next review is: price Rs 760 and market capitalisation Rs 21,067 crore; FY26 revenue Rs 3,303 crore, EBITDA Rs 1,113 crore (34%) and PAT Rs 814 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 638 crore (+6.0%), operating margin 23% and PAT Rs 109 crore (-23.8%); trailing twelve-month revenue Rs 3,339 crore and EPS Rs 28.17 [F] (NUMBERS). The disclosed order book is Rs 2,999 crore at 31 December 2025 plus Rs 1,375 crore of onboard Kavach orders secured in the quarter to February 2026 [F] (RATING). Fair values from our model are bear Rs 123.3, base Rs 239.5 and bull Rs 354.8, with a reverse-DCF implied growth requirement of 58.9% a year [F] (NUMBERS). Management's live statements to track are the Rs 3,000 crore revenue floor, Kavach at Rs 1,300-1,500 crore a year through FY28, the Rs 4,500 crore FY30 ambition, a March 2027 electric truck approval with July 2027 pilot sales, and torpedo motor sales from FY28 [MC] (CALL Sep 2025; AR2025 p.5) [F] (SCREENER).

summary.one_line: HBL Engineering is a high-quality, debt-free, approval-moated industrial whose FY26 step-change in revenue and margin came almost entirely from one railway safety programme in its execution phase, and whose share price at Rs 760 sits above the fair value implied by every scenario in our model, with the reverse DCF requiring about 59% annual sales growth for five years.
bull_points: [F] (AR2025 p.12) First Kavach OEM certified to specification v4.0 on 13 May 2025, with contracts of about Rs 4,000 crore covering 6,980 km, 2,425 locomotives, 758 stations and 460 level-crossing gates - in a market where only two of five ordered companies were qualified as at September 2025 [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

[F] (NUMBERS) FY26 revenue rose 67.9% to Rs 3,303 crore and EBITDA nearly tripled to Rs 1,113 crore, lifting ROCE to 59% and ROE to 44% on borrowings of just Rs 67 crore against Rs 2,215 crore of equity.

[E] (AR2025 p.269) The margin gain is partly structural, not just volume: the FY25 segment note shows battery margin rising from 19.5% to 23.0% and defence and aviation running at 48.6%, achieved in a year when consolidated revenue fell 12%.

[F] (AR2025 p.40; AR2025 p.268) The export franchise is compounding - standalone exports Rs 452 crore in FY25 against Rs 288 crore in FY24, with battery exports up 53.8% and defence exports up 122% - in specification-locked niches where HBL claims second place globally in industrial nickel cadmium [MC] (PPT Sep 2023).

[F] (NUMBERS) Financial quality supports the franchise: operating cash flow at 0.92x profit over five years, Rs 1,003 crore of cumulative five-year free cash flow, 73.8x interest cover, no equity issuance in a decade, no ESOP and no pledged promoter shares [F] (AR2025 p.66).
bear_points: [F] (NUMBERS) At Rs 760 the price is 53.3% above the bull-case fair value of Rs 354.8, 68.5% above the base case of Rs 239.5 and 83.8% above the bear case of Rs 123.3; the reverse DCF implies about 58.9% annual sales growth for five years against a 19.5% base-case equivalent and a 9.9% nine-year actual.

[F] (SCREENER; RATING) Roughly half of FY26 revenue was Kavach, sold to Indian Railways entities, and the buyer has already enforced its terms - HBL supplied 76% of the CLW locomotive order within the window ending mid-December 2025 and the balance stands cancelled.

[F] (NUMBERS) Earnings have already turned: quarterly operating margin ran 44%, 35%, 12% and 23% across the last four quarters, and Q1 FY27 profit fell 23.8% year on year on 6.0% sales growth, annualising to about Rs 2,552 crore against FY26's Rs 3,303 crore [E] (NUMBERS).

[MC] (AR2025 p.5) Management's own documents guide to a plateau then a decline - Kavach steady at Rs 1,300-1,500 crore a year through FY28 and dipping thereafter, with a whole-company FY30 ambition of Rs 4,500 crore, roughly 8% a year above FY26 actuals [E] (NUMBERS) - while the disclosed order book fell 33% from Rs 4,479 crore (July 2025) to Rs 2,999 crore (December 2025) [F] (RATING).

[AI] (AR2025; PPT Sep 2023) Disclosure is materially below the standard the situation requires: the company publishes no order book (the only figures come from a credit rating release), no installed capacity, no divisional financials, holds one shareholder Q&A a year, and its last investor presentation is dated September 2023 - alongside a Rs 18.95 crore profit commission to the 79-year-old Chairman and Managing Director who has explicitly decided not to appoint a single CEO successor [F] (AR2025 p.50; AR2025 p.49) [MC] (AR2025 p.3).
watch_points: The FY26 annual report circulated on 3 September 2026 and the 40th AGM held on 26 September 2026 - the FY26 segment split, the FY26 top-customer and top-five concentration, the CMD's FY26 profit commission, and any company-published order book [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

September 2026 quarter margin and profit: whether Q1 FY27's 23% operating margin and -23.8% profit growth mark a trough or a trend, and whether quarterly revenue holds above Rs 700 crore against management's Rs 3,000 crore annual floor [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

Order intake versus execution: progress on the Rs 1,375 crore of onboard Kavach orders due for execution within twelve months of the quarter to February 2026, and the next disclosed order-book figure [F] (RATING).

The railway decision on the unexecuted Kavach orders held by the three OEMs that had not qualified for v4.0 - forfeiture, re-float at original prices, or extension - and whether those OEMs obtain certification [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

New-product milestones with dates already on record: DRDO approval of the third fuze type and external certification of the proximity fuzes, torpedo motor prototypes in FY27, and the 55-tonne electric truck approval targeted for March 2027 with pilot sales in July 2027 [MC] (CALL Sep 2025) [F] (SCREENER).
guidance: No new management guidance was issued in the latest quarter in our evidence base - there is no Q1 FY27 earnings call transcript, and the most recent management commentary available is the 39th AGM of 25 September 2025 and the FY25 annual report [F] (CALL Sep 2025; AR2025).

Revenue FY26: "we are budgeting for 3000 crores in sales of this fiscal year... Budgeting is the word, I am not forecasting, we are careful not to say it is management guidance" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). Outcome: FY26 revenue Rs 3,303 crore - beaten [F] (NUMBERS).

Revenue floor: "from now on, I think it will not be lower than 3000 crores... therefore, it is the next orbit" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). Status: pending for FY27; Q1 FY27 annualises to about Rs 2,552 crore [E] (NUMBERS).

Kavach: "Kavach sales should be steady at about Rs 1,300 - Rs 1,500 crs per year during FY 26, FY27, FY28. Later they should dip. But sales of Train Management Systems / Centralised Train Control should grow, to compensate" [MC] (AR2025 p.5).
FY28: "the business in the next two fiscal years should be almost as good. Definitely and perhaps better in the next year than this year. So, there could be a decline in FY28" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).
FY30 ambition: "the current businesses could together achieve Rs 4,500 Crs in total sales in FY 2030" [MC] (AR2025 p.5), reaffirmed at the AGM as "still a reasonable number" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).
Margins: "Growth should not be expected to be uniform; margins will also fluctuate" [MC] (AR2025 p.5).

Fuzes: "Electronic Fuzes would be the second largest business by FY 2030" [MC] (AR2025 p.8); ramp-up paced to FY28 - "why I'm saying it will be FY28 is if we are at this stage today, and I'm not going to jump and produce more than I can safely deliver. I'm taking the next year for that ramp up period" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025); a third fuze type approval "might happen in a month or two" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

Torpedo motors and homing head: "Torpedo motors, we can start selling in FY28. Prototypes will go in FY27"; the homing head "will take at least three years more before we can get qualified" and is not counted in the Rs 4,500 crore FY30 projection [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).
TMS / CTC: "The number of orders will be less. Maybe it'll be 100 or 200, 300 crores a year if they want to speed up" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

Electric trucks: "The last annual report said sales could begin in October 2025. However, unexpected problems (magnets) and ideas emerged in April - June 2025. The schedule for sales is delayed by a year to October 2026" [MC] (AR2025 p.10). Subsequently: approval for 55-tonne trucks now expected by March 2027 with pilot sales targeted for July 2027 [F] (SCREENER).
Marine: HBL and Cochin Shipyard incorporated Green Maritime Propulsion Private Limited in June 2026, with initial sales expected through September 2027 subject to marine certification [F] (SCREENER).

Capex and lithium: "HBL is implementing a capex plan of about 100 crores in CY 25, to make high energy density cells in house" after an earlier Rs 40 crore pilot [F] (AR2025 p.11); on the Navy-linked lithium opportunity, "by the time this fiscal year ends, we would have invested perhaps 200 crores or less. And we will make a profit from year one" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

Capital allocation and fund-raising: "We do not want to merge. We do not want to acquire. We do not want to do anything"; surplus cash to be directed to Mittelstand Technology Partners, an AIF Category 2 fund, and to dividends [MC] (CALL Sep 2025; AR2025 p.7).

Dividend: "we are going to have another dividend in March, which is the first time... It should be about the same as now, unless something dramatic happens" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). FY26 dividend payout was 10% of profit [F] (NUMBERS) and a dividend record date fell on 8 August 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

Tariffs: asked about US tariffs, "No, there will be no impact, because our budgeted sales are above 50 crores. And all of it is not lost... our customers are those who cannot easily switch from one to the other just because of an increase in price" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

Succession: "I am going on record as saying that we are not interested in finding a single CEO. But we want to build this company into a sort of holding company structure. And each division of which there are nine... will be a virtually independent company" [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).
